title: Why Sunday
hook: most Christians gather on Sunday, the day of the resurrection; Seventh-day Adventists keep Saturday
carry: the first day, a new start

segments.voice: Yesterday, God rested on the seventh day, and your line: rest is blessed. The seventh day is Saturday. So why do churches meet on Sunday?

A town called Troas, on the coast of what's now Turkey. Evening, the first day of the week, and a group of Christians is crammed into an upstairs room lit with oil lamps. The book of Acts says: "And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them." And Paul keeps going. Until midnight. A young man named Eutychus, sitting in the window, gets sleepier and sleepier, and falls from the third story to the ground. Paul runs down, wraps his arms around him, and says, he's alive. Then everyone goes back upstairs, eats, and keeps talking until dawn. A scare with a happy ending, and it quietly shows something: Christians were already gathering on the first day of the week. Today's word is its name.
screen: `AN UPSTAIRS ROOM IN TROAS.` → `PAUL PREACHES TILL MIDNIGHT.` → `THE FIRST DAY OF THE WEEK.`

segments.voice: The Lord's Day. Why the first day? Because all four Gospels say the tomb was found empty on it. John begins: "The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre." Sunday morning. So early Christians gave that day a new name. In Revelation, John says, "I was in the Spirit on the Lord's day." In Greek, kyriake, the Lord's. The name stuck. In modern Greek, Sunday is still Kyriaki; in Spanish it's domingo, in Italian domenica, both from the Latin for the Lord's. In Russian, the word for Sunday simply means resurrection. Some early Christian writers called Sunday the eighth day. The week of creation ends on the seventh; the resurrection starts a new creation, a new first day. So for them, Sunday isn't the sabbath moved over by one. It's a new start. Later, the emperor Constantine made Sunday a legal day of rest in the Roman Empire. Not all Christians keep Sunday. Seventh-day Adventists and Seventh Day Baptists worship on Saturday, because the commandment names the seventh day, and they keep it as written. For Catholics and Orthodox Christians, Sunday worship is expected of the faithful; Protestant churches gather on it too. The day differs. The idea underneath is shared: one day, set apart.
screen: `THE TOMB, ON THE FIRST DAY.` · `KYRIAKE: THE LORD'S.` · `THE EIGHTH DAY, A NEW CREATION.` · `SOME KEEP THE SEVENTH.`

segments.voice: Look ahead at the coming week for one hour you could set apart, Sunday morning, Saturday afternoon, a weekday evening, and picture filling it with something that restores you, not chores or errands: worship, a walk, a long meal, a nap, time with someone you love. If you pray, offer that hour to God ahead of time; if you don't, simply promise it to yourself.
Lord's Day. The Christian name for Sunday, the day of the resurrection, the first day of the week. Today's word.
Your line: the first day, a new start. Not the sabbath moved over, but a new first day. That's day one hundred twenty-two.

notes: Date of the Troas meeting 'around the year 57': conventional dating of Paul's third journey; confirm or soften.
Eutychus falls 'from the third loft' (Acts 20:9); Paul says 'his life is in him' (20:10). The script says 'he's alive'. Confirm.
Constantine's Sunday law of 321 (Codex Justinianus 3.12.2): confirm.
'For Catholics and Orthodox Christians, Sunday worship is expected of the faithful': Catholic Sunday obligation; Orthodox practice described more softly. Confirm.
Seventh-day Adventists and Seventh Day Baptists described neutrally. Confirm.
